chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I took a perfume from the perfumes of the Standing Place (Maqam Ibrahim), and soil from the soil of the House (Kaaba), and seven pebbles.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Evil is what you have done. As for the soil and the pebbles, return them.'

key_terms.السُّكِّ الْمَقَامِ: The perfume/scent of the Standing Place (Maqam Ibrahim)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on taking soil, pebbles, or perfume from the Kaaba for personal use?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguished between the sanctity of the structure itself and the physical matter, ruling that while the Kaaba is a sacred sanctuary, its soil and pebbles are not inherently blessed objects to be removed for personal devotion. This hadith establishes a key Shia juristic principle that 'blessing' (barakah) is not transferred through mere physical possession of material from the site, preventing the superstition of treating the Kaaba's debris as talismans.
